<!-- pr-reviewer: 3d70df795579cc4e9aca5533bc12a2b046f989b5 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** (it is still a draft; the draft state is untouched).

What looks good
- Only `crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement.rs` changed (+12 lines, two new `Row` entries); no existing row, fixture, golden or product code is touched.
- `bad_entity_mid_data.step`: both importers refuse by name (solidcore "STEP syntax error"), mesh "no exact solid to judge against". Recorded as a refusal, which is the right triage under the Prime Directive (refused by name, not silently passed).
- `lathe_holder_offset.step`: import "agree", mesh "watertight, within tolerance", `mm_per_unit` 1.0 (millimetre file). Sound, and it matches what the bench measures.
- The test only passes if each pinned verdict string equals the measured one, so the passing run confirms the rows match the code.
- Merge with origin/main is clean (already up to date).

Local results (merged with main)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --release -p camcraft-kernel --test step_agreement` | 1 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Requested before merge
- None.

Notes (not blocking)
- Body has `Changelog: none`, `Fixes #1400`, effort line; test-only, no process files, dependencies, build.rs or snapshots touched.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
